gaps.sentence: In case of fire, ___ the nearest exit.
gaps.hint: in case of plus an emergency instruction
gaps.explanation: 'In case of' plus a noun introduces an emergency instruction with the imperative: use.

gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: He would be healthier if he ___ so much red meat.
gaps.hint: an unreal present habit, past simple
gaps.explanation: For an unreal present habit, the if-clause uses the past simple: did not eat.

gaps.sentence: If the drug ___ tested properly, the side effects would have been found earlier.
gaps.hint: passive verb in an unreal past condition
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect, here in the passive: had been.

gaps.sentence: If only I had taken that job — I ___ much happier now.
gaps.hint: mixed wish: past event, present result
gaps.explanation: 'Now' anchors the result in the present, so 'would be' is needed.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ you at the airport last week, but I was abroad.
gaps.hint: regret about a missed past meeting
gaps.explanation: Regret about something that did not happen takes 'wish' plus the past perfect: had met.
